## Projects Department Health & Safety Standards

Ref:EGY/PRJCTS/HSE/REQs

- Plant and vehicles where appropriate are to have a current certificate showing the date of the last thorough examination and test issued by a third party organization. A copy of all certification is kept in thecabof theplant orvehiclewith a copyfiled in the site offices.
- All drivcrs, opcrators and users of mechanical plant and equipment are to be competent and must hold a driving license and be certified by a third party organization for the category of plant or equipment they are operating.
- Speed limits are to be set and monitored, seat belts are worn by all drivers and operators,have an unobstructedviewout of'thewindscreen and sidewindows and that theyprohibit the use of mobile phones whilst driving/operating.
- Passengers are only to be carried on plant and vehicle where a dedicated seat is provided.
- All earthmoving plant is to be fitted with a roll over protection structure (ROPS) and falling objects protection structure (FOPS). Plant and vehicles are also to be fitted with mirrors, reversing alarms and a flashing amber beacon. The flashing amber beacon and headlights are to be switched on at all timeswhendrivingoroperatingon site.
- Plant and vehicles are to park in a secure area, clear of emergency route on firm level ground. When not in use all buckets, forks etc. are to be grounded, switched off, keys removed, parking braking applied and secured. Where there is a risk of plant of vehicles moving wheels are to be chocked.
- Operators and drivers are to wear mandatory PPE when they are out of their vehicles.
- Free climbing onto the back of delivery vehicles/dump trucks vehicles is to be prevented by providing suitable access/protection facilities (i.e. fall protection etc.).
- Plant andvehiclebeingdelivered ormoved around site are tobe secured to the bed of the lowloader using chains or other such suitable means.

## 3.20. Concrete Pumping

- >Hazards associated with concrete pumping include the following:
- Traffic/public safety hazard
- Concrete placing boom structural failure - boom falling to ground
- Electrical -power line hazard
- Reversing concrete delivery truck pedestrian hazard
- Delivery hose hazard equipment/placing boom operation hazard
- Equipment under pressure hazard
- Entanglement/entrapment hazard-being crushed in thehopper
- ·Cleaning activities presenting‘projectile’ hazards.
- In the planning for concrete pumping activities the following issues should be considered:
- Site timitations andlocalstreet access
- Concrcte pumpingunit positioning
